patients.label: 52-year-old male with colon carcinoma and a left adrenal mass

identity_evidence.quote: in a male patient who presented with a right iliac fossa mass

attribution_limitations: The abstract and case text describe the patient as male (male patient, He), while only the acknowledgments refer to her case report. The case text wording is used for documented sex; the acknowledgments pronoun is kept review_only.

The left adrenal lesion is called adrenal myelolipoma (AML) confirmed on histopathology in the abstract and confirmed on typical CT findings in the discussion, but the case text and the Fig. 6 caption give the histopathology as adrenal lipoma with haemorrhagic infarction and fat necrosis. The CT impression was suggestive of AML.

The colon tumor is called a carcinoma of the caecum in the abstract, on CT and on the colonoscopic biopsy (well-differentiated), but the resection histopathology calls it a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon; CT describes the caecal lesion with colo-colic intussusception into the ascending colon, and the Fig. 1, 2 and 5 captions say ascending colon growth. The biopsy and resection are different specimens, so the site and grade wordings are kept as separate included facts.
The adrenal lesion measures 5.5 × 5.3 cm on CT in the case text, while the discussion gives dimensions of 7.6 × 6.5 × 4.6 cm without a method or time.
Long-standing anaemia appears only inside the authors hypothesis that it may increase erythropoietin and lead to AML; no onset or duration of anaemia is stated.

Normetanephrine is called secreting, creating diagnostic confusion because other parameters were within normal limit; the tumour board decision considered the lesion as a normetanephrine secreting tumour.
The source does not explicitly tie the right hemicolectomy and the adjuvant drugs to the colon tumor, so the oncology treatments carry no tumor reference.
